analyst.summary: MSWIL is India's dominant wiring-harness supplier (40%+ share, 50%+ in PV) inside a genuine structural growth category -- EV/SUV content-per-vehicle running 1.5-2.4x ICE/sedan levels -- and just posted FY26 revenue of Rs 11,477.58 cr (+23.1% YoY, first time past Rs 10,000 cr), well ahead of ~11% industry PV volume growth. But PAT grew only ~3% (Rs 625.18 cr) as operating margin slid to 8.23% in Q4 FY26 (from 14.0% in FY21) on a copper cost pass-through lag plus greenfield-plant under-utilisation (Gujarat/Maharashtra/Haryana lines still ramping toward a 65-70% utilisation target by H1 FY27). At ~40-42x trailing earnings and ~12x book, the stock is priced for that margin recovery to show up on schedule -- FY26's own numbers are the first real test of that thesis and, on the earnings line, did not yet confirm it. Real ROCE (~44.9%) and ROE (33-40% band) remain genuinely excellent -- the scraped roce=136.9%/roe=66029% are book-equity-base artefacts, not the true read -- and the balance sheet carries no red flags (D/E 0.11, zero governance concerns found). Maruti Suzuki concentration (~35-40% of revenue) is a real, uninsulated customer-risk. Net: Hold -- a genuine quality franchise with a real structural tailwind, but fully priced against an earnings-growth story that has not yet delivered, so no fresh conviction to add and no red flag to force an exit either.
